segmentation.text: No pedestrian
shall cross a roadway
other than in a marked crosswalk or within an unmarked crosswalk
in any business district

elements.justification: 'Pedestrian' is admitted as the aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian ('a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair, or a person on an electric personal assistive mobility device'); ru.aggregate carries 'membership of a legal aggregate' and is claimed as one atom, never expanded into classes. Same words, same atoms as 'No pedestrian' in LVMC_11_30_050.

Same words, same mapping as LVMC_11_30_050. 'a roadway' (DEF-NRS-484A-220: 'that portion of a highway which is improved and ordinarily used for vehicular traffic, exclusive of the shoulder') is st.roadway, 'the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic, excluding shoulder'; its exclusion (not the sidewalk) does not apply, since only the roadway is read. The pedestrian is on it by rel.occupies ('a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region'). 'cross' is motion across the designated direction of travel of a lane ('a longitudinal strip of roadway for one line of vehicles') or of the roadway the pedestrian occupies: drv.motion.moving_across_carrier ('Road user a moves across the designated direction of travel of carrier region r'); that concept says nothing of occupancy, so occupancy is read beside it. st.lane is not used as a half of the roadway or a lateral position, as its exclusion forbids: only as a carrier of a direction.

'a marked crosswalk or ... an unmarked crosswalk' (DEF-NRS-484A-065: '(1) That part of a highway at an intersection included within the connections of the lateral lines of the sidewalks ... or (2) Any portion of a highway at an intersection or elsewhere distinctly indicated for pedestrian crossing by lines or other markings on the surface') is st.crosswalk: 'marked crossing, or the unmarked prolongation of sidewalks at an intersection (st.intersection); marked attribute'. Both values of the marked attribute are admitted, so the definition's whole extent is kept. 'in' / 'within' is the footprint overlapping the crosswalk: rel.occupies. Same atoms as 'except in a crosswalk' (LVMC_11_30_050).

assumptions.meaning: the place of the road user at the observation lies in a business district, as the map's reading classifies the area

applicability: The subject is a pedestrian (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian) whose footprint overlaps a roadway (rel.occupies, st.roadway) at a place the reading declares to lie in a business district (asm.business_district), read at the judged observation.
obligation: At every observation at which the subject occupies a roadway and moves across a lane or roadway it occupies (drv.motion.moving_across_carrier with speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance and cos_max p.crossing_motion_cos, on a region of kind st.lane or st.roadway the subject occupies), the subject's footprint overlaps a crosswalk (rel.occupies, st.crosswalk, marked or unmarked). Moving across the roadway while occupying no crosswalk is violated; standing on the roadway or moving along it is not a crossing and is compliant here.

narrowings.why: 'cross a roadway' is read at each observation as moving across the designated direction of a lane or roadway the pedestrian occupies (more than p.crossing_motion_cos from it, faster than p.halt_speed_tolerance); a pedestrian standing on the roadway or walking along it is not crossing and is not judged by this rule (LVMC_11_30_090 judges walking along).

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian (ru.pedestrian) moves at 1.4 m/s across a lane at right angles to the lane's st.lane_direction, footprint on the roadway and on no st.crosswalk, at a place declared asm.business_district true.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same pedestrian crosses the same roadway with its footprint inside a st.crosswalk with marked true at every observation of the crossing, in a business district.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian walks on a st.sidewalk and occupies no roadway, in a business district.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian is on the roadway outside any crosswalk in a business district; the source does not observe kin.velocity, so whether it moves across the lane is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The pedestrian crosses within an unmarked crosswalk (st.crosswalk with marked false) at an intersection, in a business district.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: The pedestrian crosses mid-block outside any crosswalk at a place declared asm.business_district false.

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed quantisation of the acquisition standard's scene graph

param_proposals.name: p.crossing_motion_cos
param_proposals.convention: largest absolute cosine between a pedestrian's velocity and a carrier's designated direction at which the pedestrian counts as moving across the carrier rather than along it: motion more than about 20 degrees away from the direction of travel
param_proposals.source: pedestrian crossing-trajectory observation studies (FHWA pedestrian crossing behaviour)

segmentation.text: Where sidewalks are provided
it shall be unlawful for any pedestrian
to walk along and upon an adjacent roadway

elements.justification: 'sidewalks' (DEF-NRS-484A-240: 'that portion of a highway between the curb lines or the lateral lines of a highway and the adjacent property lines intended for the use of pedestrians') is st.sidewalk, 'area for pedestrians between roadway and property line'; it is not read as a crosswalk, its exclusion. 'provided' is the sidewalk's presence on the map (an observable_reading of category status). The sidewalk is tied to the place of the duty by st.on_way ('the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on'): the sidewalk lies on the highway (st.highway, 'the entire public way between its boundary lines, including sidewalks and shoulders') on which the roadway the pedestrian occupies lies. st.on_way is not read as nearness to a way, its exclusion: both regions are recorded as lying on that highway.

'any pedestrian' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian ('a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair, or a person on an electric personal assistive mobility device'), one atom, never expanded; same atoms as 'Any pedestrian' (LVMC_11_30_060_B). 'it shall be unlawful for' states the prohibition the obligation span describes.

'upon ... roadway' (DEF-NRS-484A-220: 'that portion of a highway which is improved and ordinarily used for vehicular traffic, exclusive of the shoulder') is the footprint overlapping st.roadway ('the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic, excluding shoulder'; not the sidewalk, which is not read here): rel.occupies. 'adjacent' ties that roadway to the sidewalks of s1: the roadway lies on the same highway (st.on_way, st.highway). 'walk along' is moving (not drv.motion.complete_halt: the road user is not at rest) and not moving across the designated direction of the lane (st.lane) or roadway it occupies (not drv.motion.moving_across_carrier, 'Road user a moves across the designated direction of travel of carrier region r'): with the same tolerance that separates crossing from walking along in LVMC_11_30_050, motion within that angle of the direction of travel is along it. st.lane serves as a carrier of a direction only, never as a half of the roadway, its exclusion.

applicability: The subject is a pedestrian (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian) whose footprint overlaps a roadway r (rel.occupies, st.roadway) that lies on a highway h (st.on_way, st.highway) on which a sidewalk (st.sidewalk) also lies (st.on_way), read at the judged observation.
obligation: At every such observation, for every roadway r the subject occupies that lies on a highway on which a sidewalk lies (re-bound with the whole selection), the subject does not walk along r: it is violated where the subject is not at rest (not drv.motion.complete_halt with speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance) and, for a lane or roadway carrier c of r that it occupies (st.lane on the same highway, or r itself), it is not moving across c (not drv.motion.moving_across_carrier with speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance and cos_max p.crossing_motion_cos); at rest or moving across the roadway is compliant.

narrowings.why: A sidewalk is 'provided' where the map records one lying on the same highway as the roadway the pedestrian occupies (st.on_way); its presence is the evidence that it was provided. A sidewalk on either side of the highway counts.

'walk along' is read as moving faster than p.halt_speed_tolerance and not across the occupied carrier's designated direction by more than the angle p.crossing_motion_cos sets; 'walk' is read for every member of the pedestrian aggregate (a person in a wheelchair included) as its motion. 'adjacent' is read as lying on the same highway as a sidewalk (st.on_way); no relation atom states adjacency more narrowly.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian (ru.pedestrian) walks at 1.4 m/s along a lane, velocity parallel to its st.lane_direction, footprint on the roadway; a st.sidewalk lies on the same st.highway (st.on_way).

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: On the same roadway the pedestrian walks across the lane at right angles to its st.lane_direction (drv.motion.moving_across_carrier holds).

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian walks along a lane of a roadway whose highway carries no st.sidewalk (no sidewalk lies on it).

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian moves on the roadway beside which a sidewalk lies; the source does not observe kin.velocity, so whether it moves along or across the lane is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian stands at rest on the roadway (kin.speed at or below p.halt_speed_tolerance), a sidewalk lying on the same highway.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian walks along the sidewalk and occupies no roadway.

param_proposals.source: speed quantisation of the acquisition standard's scene graph

segmentation.text: Any pedestrian who is not wholly or partially blind
or any driver of any vehicle
who approaches or comes in contact with
a person wholly or partially blind, carrying a cane or walking stick white in color, or white tipped in red, or being assisted by a person
with wisdom
shall immediately
come to a full stop
and take such precautions before proceeding
as may be necessary to avoid an accident or injury to the person wholly or partially blind

elements.justification: 'pedestrian' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian ('a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair, or a person on an electric personal assistive mobility device'). 'who is not wholly or partially blind' leaves out the pedestrians the law protects; blindness itself is no observable, and is read through the feature the same sentence names as its sign: the subject is not of the class ru.pedestrian_with_white_cane_or_guide_animal ('pedestrian carrying a white or white-and-red cane, accompanied by a guide animal, or led by another person'), which carries no exclusion of its own.

'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway', with its exclusions of devices moved by human power, electric bicycles, electric personal assistive mobility devices and electric scooters, which the reading classifies). 'driver' (DEF-NRS-484A-080) is the role of who controls the vehicle, never membership: it is read through the vehicle's controlled motion. Same atoms as 'The driver of a vehicle' (LVMC_11_20_060_o1).

'comes in contact with' is rel.contact, 'the bodies of two road users ... touch or overlap (a collision)', taken at the observation at which it begins; a near miss is not contact, its exclusion, and is read by 'approaches'. 'approaches' is the subject, while not at rest (not drv.motion.complete_halt), coming within a reach of the person: the centre-to-centre distance (rel.centre_distance, 'Euclidean ground-plane distance between reference points') falls to p.blind_person_approach_reach. That atom is not read as a clearance between bodies or an order of arrival, its exclusions: only as how near the subject has come.

The person protected is identified by the features the words list: 'carrying a cane or walking stick white in color, or white tipped in red, or being assisted by a person' is ru.pedestrian_with_white_cane_or_guide_animal, 'pedestrian carrying a white or white-and-red cane, accompanied by a guide animal, or led by another person'. 'a person wholly or partially blind' with those features is the pedestrian the class describes: the ontology's class for exactly this description, whose contract states no exclusion. The person is another road user than the subject, quantified in the applicability.

'stop' is required here, so DEF-NRS-484A-255 applies by its own scope ('when required, means complete cessation from movement'; DEF-NRS-484A-260 is scoped to stopping 'when prohibited'). 'come to a full stop' is drv.motion.complete_halt, whose contract quotes that definition: 'The road user is at rest at the observation — complete cessation from movement'.

operationalizations.convention: The stop is immediate when the subject is at rest within a window ahead of the approach or contact event no longer than a perception-reaction time plus the braking time from an urban approach speed (AASHTO stopping-sight-distance model).

residues.why: 'with wisdom' qualifies the person assisting, not the person protected; that the person assisted is wholly or partially blind and is being assisted is what identifies the protected person, and a helper's wisdom, a state of mind no trace shows, does not change that identification, so the duty owed to the person assisted is the same whether or not the helper's wisdom holds.

applicability: The subject is either a pedestrian (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian) that is not of the class ru.pedestrian_with_white_cane_or_guide_animal, or a vehicle (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) read through its controlled motion; and at the judged observation, for some other road user b of the scene (not the same as the subject) of the class ru.pedestrian_with_white_cane_or_guide_animal, an approach or contact event occurs: rel.contact between the subject and b holds here and did not at the previous observation, or rel.centre_distance between them is at most p.blind_person_approach_reach here and was not at the previous observation while the subject is not at rest (not drv.motion.complete_halt with speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance).
obligation: At each observation at which such an event occurs, the subject is at rest (drv.motion.complete_halt with speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance) at some observation of the window ahead of length p.immediate_stop_window, measured in time on the subject. No halt in that window is violated; a window that reaches past the end of the trace without a halt is unknown.

narrowings.why: 'driver of any vehicle' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the duty binds the vehicle's conduct whoever or whatever controls it.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A motor vehicle (ru.motor_vehicle) moving at 10 m/s comes within p.blind_person_approach_reach (rel.centre_distance) of a ru.pedestrian_with_white_cane_or_guide_animal at the kerb and keeps moving: no observation of the window p.immediate_stop_window ahead has kin.speed at or below p.halt_speed_tolerance.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same vehicle decelerates and is at rest (drv.motion.complete_halt) within p.immediate_stop_window after the centre distance first falls to the reach.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A vehicle drives past an ordinary pedestrian (ru.pedestrian, no cane, not led); no road user of class ru.pedestrian_with_white_cane_or_guide_animal is in the scene.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A ru.pedestrian_with_white_cane_or_guide_animal stands near the vehicle's path; rel.centre_distance is not observed and no contact occurs, so whether the vehicle approached is unknown; the vehicle does not halt.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The subject is itself a ru.pedestrian_with_white_cane_or_guide_animal walking toward another such pedestrian.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian (ru.pedestrian, no cane) walking comes into rel.contact with a ru.pedestrian_with_white_cane_or_guide_animal and keeps walking, never at rest within p.immediate_stop_window.

param_proposals.name: p.blind_person_approach_reach
param_proposals.convention: the centre distance within which a moving road user has approached a pedestrian carrying a white cane or led by another person: the stopping distance from an urban approach speed of about 13 m/s with a 1 s perception-reaction time and a 4.5 m/s^2 deceleration
param_proposals.source: AASHTO A Policy on Geometric Design of Highways and Streets, stopping-sight-distance model

param_proposals.name: p.immediate_stop_window
param_proposals.convention: the longest time from the moment a stop is due until the road user is at rest for the stop to be immediate: a 1 s perception-reaction time plus the braking time from an urban approach speed of about 13 m/s at 4.5 m/s^2
param_proposals.source: AASHTO A Policy on Geometric Design of Highways and Streets, stopping-sight-distance model

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed quantisation of the acquisition standard's scene graph

segmentation.text: Any pedestrian who is not wholly or partially blind
or any driver of any vehicle
who approaches or comes in contact with
a person wholly or partially blind, carrying a cane or walking stick white in color, or white tipped in red, or being assisted by a person
with wisdom
shall immediately
come to a full stop
and take such precautions before proceeding
as may be necessary to avoid an accident or injury to the person wholly or partially blind

elements.justification: 'pedestrian' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian ('a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair, or a person on an electric personal assistive mobility device'). 'who is not wholly or partially blind' leaves out the pedestrians the law protects; blindness itself is no observable, and is read through the feature the same sentence names as its sign: the subject is not of the class ru.pedestrian_with_white_cane_or_guide_animal ('pedestrian carrying a white or white-and-red cane, accompanied by a guide animal, or led by another person'), which carries no exclusion of its own.

'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway', with its exclusions of devices moved by human power, electric bicycles, electric personal assistive mobility devices and electric scooters, which the reading classifies). 'driver' (DEF-NRS-484A-080) is the role of who controls the vehicle, never membership: it is read through the vehicle's controlled motion. Same atoms as 'The driver of a vehicle' (LVMC_11_20_060_o1).

'comes in contact with' is rel.contact, 'the bodies of two road users ... touch or overlap (a collision)', taken at the observation at which it begins; a near miss is not contact, its exclusion, and is read by 'approaches'. 'approaches' is the subject, while not at rest (not drv.motion.complete_halt), coming within a reach of the person: the centre-to-centre distance (rel.centre_distance, 'Euclidean ground-plane distance between reference points') falls to p.blind_person_approach_reach. That atom is not read as a clearance between bodies or an order of arrival, its exclusions: only as how near the subject has come.

The person protected is identified by the features the words list: 'carrying a cane or walking stick white in color, or white tipped in red, or being assisted by a person' is ru.pedestrian_with_white_cane_or_guide_animal, 'pedestrian carrying a white or white-and-red cane, accompanied by a guide animal, or led by another person'. 'a person wholly or partially blind' with those features is the pedestrian the class describes: the ontology's class for exactly this description, whose contract states no exclusion. The person is another road user than the subject, quantified in the applicability.

'before proceeding' refers to the full stop the sibling span requires after the approach or contact (o1): proceeding is the subject moving again (not drv.motion.complete_halt) after it has been at rest (drv.motion.complete_halt, 'The road user is at rest at the observation — complete cessation from movement', DEF-NRS-484A-255, the definition scoped to a stop 'when required') since the latest approach or contact event with the same protected person. The referent keeps its subject (this subject), its object (that person), its event and its order (halt after the event, motion after the halt). 'take such precautions' is read through the outcome the precautions secure (observable_reading, perception), which the standard span bounds.

operationalizations.standard: such precautions ... as may be necessary to avoid an accident or injury to the person wholly or partially blind
operationalizations.convention: Traffic-conflict technique: while proceeding, the subject neither touches the protected person (rel.contact) nor is on a course whose closest approach of centres, under constant velocities, comes within p.conflict_horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) at a distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance); an accident or injury is avoided when no such contact or conflict arises.

residues.why: 'with wisdom' qualifies the person assisting, not the person protected; that the person assisted is wholly or partially blind and is being assisted is what identifies the protected person, and a helper's wisdom, a state of mind no trace shows, does not change that identification, so the duty owed to the person assisted is the same whether or not the helper's wisdom holds.

applicability: The subject is either a pedestrian (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian) that is not of the class ru.pedestrian_with_white_cane_or_guide_animal, or a vehicle (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) read through its controlled motion; for some other road user b (not the same as the subject) of the class ru.pedestrian_with_white_cane_or_guide_animal, an approach or contact event (rel.contact beginning, or rel.centre_distance first falling to at most p.blind_person_approach_reach while the subject is not at rest) occurred at or before the judged observation; the subject has been at rest (drv.motion.complete_halt with speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance) at some observation since the latest such event; and at the judged observation the subject is not at rest (proceeding).
obligation: At every such observation, for that b: the subject is not in contact with b (rel.contact), and it is not the case that the centres of the subject and b approach each other within p.conflict_horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) with a closest-approach distance (prim.closest_approach_distance, same horizon) below p.conflict_centre_clearance. Either contact or such a conflict course is violated. Surrogate: the verdict is evidence for the standard, not a legal conclusion.

narrowings.why: 'driver of any vehicle' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the duty binds the vehicle's conduct whoever or whatever controls it.
'take such precautions' is a duty to make sure, read through the outcome it secures while the subject proceeds after its stop: no contact with and no conflict course toward the protected person.
'an accident or injury' is read only through contact between the bodies and a predicted closest approach of the centres below the clearance within the horizon; an injury without contact is not read.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A motor vehicle comes within the reach of a ru.pedestrian_with_white_cane_or_guide_animal crossing ahead, halts, then moves off toward the pedestrian: prim.closest_approach_within holds over p.conflict_horizon with prim.closest_approach_distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The vehicle halts, waits until the pedestrian has left its path, then moves off; the centres do not approach below the clearance within the horizon and no rel.contact occurs.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A vehicle halts and moves off near an ordinary pedestrian; no ru.pedestrian_with_white_cane_or_guide_animal is in the scene.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A vehicle halts and moves off near a ru.pedestrian_with_white_cane_or_guide_animal; rel.centre_distance is not observed and no contact occurs, so whether an approach event occurred is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: After halting, the vehicle moves off and its body touches the white-cane pedestrian (rel.contact).

param_proposals.convention: the centre distance within which a moving road user has approached a pedestrian carrying a white cane or led by another person: the stopping distance from an urban approach speed of about 13 m/s with a 1 s perception-reaction time and a 4.5 m/s^2 deceleration
param_proposals.source: AASHTO A Policy on Geometric Design of Highways and Streets, stopping-sight-distance model

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_horizon
param_proposals.convention: time-to-collision threshold of the traffic-conflict technique: a closest approach later than this is not a present danger of a crash

param_proposals.convention: centre-to-centre distance at the closest approach below which the bodies of a passenger car and another road user are taken to collide or nearly collide: about a car's half-length plus half a body width
param_proposals.source: AASHTO passenger-car design vehicle dimensions

segmentation.text: No motorcycle
or motor scooter
shall be ridden
upon any sidewalk
of the City

elements.justification: 'motorcycle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-135::motorcycle ('every motor vehicle equipped with a seat or saddle for the use of the driver and designed to travel on not more than three wheels in contact with the ground, excluding an electric bicycle, a tractor or a moped'), one atom, never replaced by ru.motorcycle.

No definition applies to 'motor scooter'. A seated motor-driven scooter is either a motor vehicle on not more than three wheels with a seat, already a member of the motorcycle aggregate of s1, or a small-engined scooter that DEF-NRS-484A-125 names as a 'motor-driven scooter', which the motorcycle definition excludes as a moped: ru.moped, 'a low-power two- or three-wheeler with a small engine or motor, as a jurisdiction classes it'. The standing electric scooter (ru.electric_scooter) is not a 'motor scooter' of this chapter: the code defines and regulates 'electric scooter' separately (DEF-LVMC-11-02-083, chapter 11.40).

'be ridden' is the machine in controlled motion: not drv.motion.complete_halt ('The road user is at rest at the observation — complete cessation from movement', speed at or below a tolerance). A motorcycle at rest on a sidewalk is not ridden. Who rides is read through the machine's motion (observable_reading, agency).

'sidewalk' (DEF-NRS-484A-240: 'that portion of a highway between the curb lines or the lateral lines of a highway and the adjacent property lines intended for the use of pedestrians') is st.sidewalk, 'area for pedestrians between roadway and property line'; not a crosswalk, its exclusion. 'upon any' is the footprint overlapping it: rel.occupies ('a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region (... sidewalk ...)').

applicability: The subject is a motorcycle (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-135::motorcycle) or a moped (ru.moped) whose footprint overlaps a sidewalk (rel.occupies, st.sidewalk) at a place the reading declares within the city's limits (asm.within_city_limits), read at the judged observation.
obligation: At every such observation the subject is at rest (drv.motion.complete_halt with speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance); moving while on the sidewalk is violated.

narrowings.why: 'be ridden' is read through the machine's controlled motion (not at rest); whether a person sits on it or pushes it is not told apart.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A motorcycle (ru.motorcycle) moves at 3 m/s with its footprint on a st.sidewalk, at a place declared asm.within_city_limits true.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: A motorcycle stands at rest (kin.speed at or below p.halt_speed_tolerance) on a sidewalk within the city.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A motorcycle moves on the roadway and occupies no sidewalk.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A motorcycle is on a sidewalk within the city; the source does not observe kin.speed.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A moped (ru.moped) moves at 2 m/s on a sidewalk within the city.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: A motorcycle moves on a sidewalk at a place declared asm.within_city_limits false.

segmentation.text: All vehicles
covered under this Section, as provided in Section 11.38.080

shall carry at least one lighted headlamp capable of showing a white light visible at least three hundred feet in the direction in which the same are proceeding, and one tail lamp mounted on the rear which, when lighted, shall emit a red light plainly visible from at least five hundred feet to the rear
The lights required by this Section shall be burning
whenever such vehicles are in motion
during the period from one-half hour after sunset to one-half hour before sunrise

and at any other time when, due to insufficient light or unfavorable atmospheric conditions, persons and vehicles on the streets are not clearly discernible at a distance of at least five hundred feet ahead

elements.justification: 'vehicles' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway', with its listed exclusions), one atom, never expanded.

Nearest atoms only, to show why the span is a gap: sig.headlamp ('headlamp state ∈ {off, low_beam, high_beam}') and sig.position_lamp ('position, parking, cowl or tail lamps lit') denote whether a lamp is lit at an observation. The duty is one of equipment: that the vehicle carries a white front lamp whose light is visible at the stated distance ahead and a rear-mounted red tail lamp visible from the stated distance behind, lit or not. No atom denotes a vehicle's lamp equipment, its colour, its mounting or the distance at which its light is visible.

residues.why: A reference to LVMC 11.38.080, a section outside the corpus (no bracketed id resolves it): which vehicles that section covers is not stated in any line of the corpus, so the rule binds every member of the vehicle aggregate.

applicability: The subject is a vehicle (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle), at every observation.
obligation: At every observation the subject is equipped with at least one front headlamp able to show a white light visible at least 300 ft ahead and one tail lamp mounted on the rear able to emit, when lit, a red light visible from at least 500 ft behind. Not statable with the ontology: the gap on s3.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A motorcycle whose equipment record (the proposed lamp-equipment atom) shows no rear tail lamp.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: A motorcycle equipped with a white headlamp visible 120 m ahead and a red rear tail lamp visible 160 m behind.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle (ru.bicycle, excluded from the vehicle aggregate as a device moved by human power) is the only road user.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A motorcycle whose lamps the source does not observe at all.

gaps.proposal: `ru.lamp_equipment` | the lamps a vehicle is equipped with, lit or not: per lamp, **position** ∈ {front, rear, side}, **colour** ∈ {white, red, amber, other}, and the distance at which its light, when lit, is visible in clear air (m), as the source's equipment record or inspection states **Not a stand-in for:** a lamp lit at the observation (`sig.headlamp`, `sig.position_lamp`) | general — it decides the equipment the law requires a vehicle to carry: which lamps, where mounted, of what colour and of what visible range

segmentation.text: All vehicles
covered under this Section, as provided in Section 11.38.080

shall carry at least one lighted headlamp capable of showing a white light visible at least three hundred feet in the direction in which the same are proceeding, and one tail lamp mounted on the rear which, when lighted, shall emit a red light plainly visible from at least five hundred feet to the rear
The lights required by this Section shall be burning
whenever such vehicles are in motion
during the period from one-half hour after sunset to one-half hour before sunrise

and at any other time when, due to insufficient light or unfavorable atmospheric conditions, persons and vehicles on the streets are not clearly discernible at a distance of at least five hundred feet ahead

elements.justification: 'vehicles' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway', with its listed exclusions), one atom, never expanded.

'The lights required by this Section' refers to the lamps of s3: at least one headlamp and one tail lamp mounted on the rear. 'burning' is their being lit: the headlamp by sig.headlamp ('headlamp state ∈ {off, low_beam, high_beam}') in a state other than off, the tail lamp by sig.position_lamp ('position, parking, cowl or tail lamps lit (the lamps a vehicle shows without its headlamps)'). The lamps' colour and visible range are the equipment duty of s3, not the duty to have them burning.
'such vehicles' are the subject; 'in motion' is not at rest: not drv.motion.complete_halt ('The road user is at rest at the observation — complete cessation from movement').

env.darkness is 'insufficient natural light; the boundary relative to sunset and sunrise is a reading parameter': the period from half an hour after sunset to half an hour before sunrise is that atom with its boundary set by the reading at the figure the words state.

'not clearly discernible at a distance of at least five hundred feet ahead' is the visibility distance (env.visibility, 'visibility distance (fog, dust, smoke)') below the stated figure, whatever the 'unfavorable atmospheric conditions' causing it; 'insufficient light' is env.darkness ('insufficient natural light'). 'persons and vehicles on the streets' names what must be discernible; the visibility distance is the distance at which any object is discernible, so it carries them.

residues.why: A reference to LVMC 11.38.080, a section outside the corpus (no bracketed id resolves it): which vehicles that section covers is not stated in any line of the corpus, so the rule binds every member of the vehicle aggregate.

applicability: The subject is a vehicle (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) that is not at rest (not drv.motion.complete_halt with speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance) at an observation at which env.darkness holds or env.visibility is below 500 ft.
obligation: At every such observation the subject's headlamp is lit (sig.headlamp in state low_beam or high_beam) and its tail lamps are lit (sig.position_lamp); either one not lit is violated.

narrowings.why: The tail lamp is read through sig.position_lamp, which groups position, parking, cowl and tail lamps: a lit position lamp other than a tail lamp is not told apart from a lit tail lamp.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A motorcycle moves at 10 m/s with env.darkness true; sig.headlamp is off and sig.position_lamp is lit.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same motorcycle at night with sig.headlamp low_beam and sig.position_lamp lit.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A motorcycle moves in daylight (env.darkness false) with env.visibility of 2000 m.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A motorcycle moves at night; the source does not observe sig.headlamp; sig.position_lamp is lit.

scenarios.name: branch_2

segmentation.text: Any person operating a bicycle, electric bicycle, or electric scooter
shall obey the instructions of official traffic-control signals, signs and other control devices applicable to vehicles
unless otherwise directed by a Police Officer

elements.justification: 'bicycle' (DEF-NRS-484A-025, 'a device propelled by human power upon which a person may ride'), 'electric bicycle' (DEF-LVMC-11-02-082) and 'electric scooter' (DEF-LVMC-11-02-083) are admitted aggregates, each claimed as one atom. 'Any person operating' is read through the machine's controlled motion (agency).

Nearest atoms only, to show why the span is a gap. The devices are carried: dev.traffic_signal ('a signal head; state ...'), dev.stop_sign, dev.yield_sign, dev.regulatory_sign ('a point regulation by catalogue code'), dev.lane_control_signal, tied to the subject's region by dev.governs ('the travel regions whose traffic the device controls') and rel.occupies; 'vehicles' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle. What none carries is 'the instructions ... applicable to vehicles': the conduct each device requires of a vehicle is stated by the vehicle rules of the corpus, and a composed rule is engaged only for a road user of its binders' classes, while a bicycle, an electric bicycle and an electric scooter are excluded from the vehicle aggregate ('Devices moved by human power', 'Electric bicycles', 'An electric scooter').

'directed by a Police Officer' is dev.human_direction ('a person directing traffic and the direction given; role ∈ {police_officer, ...}; indication ∈ {stop, proceed, slow, turn(dir)}') with role police_officer, governing (dev.governs) a travel region the subject occupies (rel.occupies, st.travel_region); 'otherwise' is an indication given to the subject's region. The officer's authority is read from the role displayed (status). Same pattern as the flagman exception of LVMC_11_16_030.

applicability: The subject is a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter in controlled motion, occupying a travel region (rel.occupies, st.travel_region) that an official traffic-control device governs (dev.governs), and no police officer (dev.human_direction with role police_officer) governing that region gives it a direction.
obligation: At every such observation the subject complies with every rule of the corpus stating the instruction such a device gives to vehicles, read for the subject as though it were a vehicle. Not statable: the operator gap on s2.

narrowings.why: 'operating' is read through the machine's controlled motion, whoever or whatever controls it.
'official' is read from the device's presence on the road: its official status is presumed.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle (ru.bicycle) on a lane governed (dev.governs) by a traffic signal displaying circular_red enters the intersection; no police officer directs.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The bicycle halts at the stop line and stays out of the intersection until the signal displays circular_green.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle rides on a lane that no device governs.

scenarios.name: blind

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A police officer (dev.human_direction, role police_officer, indication proceed) governing the bicycle's lane waves it into the intersection while the signal displays circular_red.

gaps.proposal: `ruleAsClass` (id, map, aggregate): another rule complied with by the mapped road users, its subject binder's class condition read as the named aggregate instead of its own, so that a duty the words make applicable to vehicles binds a road user of another class (a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter) — it decides the action the law requires: the instructions each official traffic-control device gives vehicles, owed by a road user the vehicle aggregate excludes
gaps.nearest: Formula.rule (another rule complied with; 'not engaged counts as complied'): a vehicle rule composed for a bicycle is never engaged, its binder's class failing, so it reports compliance whatever the bicycle does; dev.traffic_signal, dev.stop_sign, dev.regulatory_sign, dev.governs carry the devices and their states, not the conduct they require of a vehicle

segmentation.text: Whenever authorized signs are erected indicating that no right turn, left turn or U-turn is permitted
it shall be unlawful for any person operating a bicycle, electric bicycle, or electric scooter
to disobey the direction of any such sign
except where such person dismounts from the bicycle, electric bicycle, or electric scooter to make any such turn
in which event such person shall then obey the regulations applicable to pedestrians

elements.justification: 'signs ... indicating that no right turn, left turn or U-turn is permitted' are dev.regulatory_sign ('a point regulation by catalogue code') with code no_right_turn, no_left_turn or no_u_turn; a prohibition sign is a condition, not a manoeuvre, as its exclusion states, and the manoeuvre is read by the turn concepts of s3. The sign applies to the subject where it governs (dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls', a lane, roadway or intersection among them) a travel region (st.travel_region) the subject's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) while the turn is under way. 'authorized ... erected' is read from the sign's presence (status).

'bicycle' (DEF-NRS-484A-025, 'a device propelled by human power upon which a person may ride'), 'electric bicycle' (DEF-LVMC-11-02-082) and 'electric scooter' (DEF-LVMC-11-02-083) are admitted aggregates, each claimed as one atom. 'any person operating' is read through the machine's controlled motion (agency); 'it shall be unlawful for' states the prohibition.

'disobey the direction of any such sign' is making the turn the sign singled out in s1 prohibits: under no_right_turn a right turn (drv.motion.right_turn, 'Road user a has completed a turn to the right'), under no_left_turn a left turn (drv.motion.left_turn), under no_u_turn a U-turn (drv.motion.u_turn, after DEF-NRS-484B-077 'the turning of a vehicle upon a highway so as to proceed in the opposite direction'). The sign's code selects which act is forbidden.

'dismounts from the bicycle ... to make any such turn' is the person making the turn afoot: the road user is a member of the pedestrian aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian ('a person afoot') while the turn (the same turn concepts as s3) is under way. A person walking beside the machine is afoot, not riding it.

applicability: The subject is a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter in controlled motion whose footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) a travel region (st.travel_region) governed (dev.governs) by a regulatory sign (dev.regulatory_sign) of code no_right_turn, no_left_turn or no_u_turn.
obligation: At each observation at which a turn of the subject is recognized — drv.motion.right_turn, drv.motion.left_turn or drv.motion.u_turn, each with window p.turn_window, the heading thresholds p.turn_heading_min and p.u_turn_heading_min (u_turn: p.u_turn_heading_min only) and yaw_tol p.turn_yaw_rate_tol — it is violated where, at some observation of the window p.turn_window behind at which the turn is under way (|kin.yaw_rate| above p.turn_yaw_rate_tol), the subject occupied a travel region governed by a sign whose code prohibits that turn (no_right_turn for a right turn, no_left_turn for a left turn, no_u_turn for a U-turn), unless the subject was a member of the pedestrian aggregate (afoot) at every observation of that window at which the turn was under way; otherwise compliant.

narrowings.why: 'authorized signs are erected' is read from the sign's presence on the road: its authorization is presumed.
'operating' is read through the machine's controlled motion, whoever or whatever controls it.

scenarios.name: forbid

scenarios.name: blind

scenarios.name: occasion_s1_outside

scenarios.name: branch_1

under_way.justification: An observation inside the turn is one of the window behind its recognition at which the subject's heading is turning: the magnitude of kin.yaw_rate ('rate of change of heading') above p.turn_yaw_rate_tol. A place alone does not tell it, since the subject occupied the same regions before it began to turn; kin.yaw_rate is not read as road curvature, its exclusion: it is the subject's own heading change.

segmentation.text: Whenever a
usable
path for bicycles, electric bicycles, or electric scooters has been provided
adjacent to a roadway
riders of bicycles, electric bicycles, and electric scooters
shall use such path and shall not use the roadway

elements.justification: 'path for bicycles, electric bicycles, or electric scooters' is st.bicycle_lane_or_path, 'lane or separate path reserved for bicycles and the devices a jurisdiction groups with them': the classes the path is for are those the kind is reserved for. 'has been provided' is its presence on the map (status). It lies on a highway (st.on_way, 'the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on'; st.highway).

'adjacent to a roadway' ties the path to the roadway (DEF-NRS-484A-220, 'that portion of a highway which is improved and ordinarily used for vehicular traffic, exclusive of the shoulder'; st.roadway, 'the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic, excluding shoulder') through the highway both lie on (st.on_way, st.highway); st.on_way is not read as nearness, its exclusion: both regions are recorded on that highway.

'bicycles' (DEF-NRS-484A-025, 'a device propelled by human power upon which a person may ride'), 'electric bicycles' (DEF-LVMC-11-02-082) and 'electric scooters' (DEF-LVMC-11-02-083) are admitted aggregates, each claimed as one atom. 'riders' is read through the machine's controlled motion (agency).

'use such path' is the rider's footprint on the path singled out by s3 (rel.occupies, st.bicycle_lane_or_path); 'not use the roadway' is the rider not travelling along that roadway (rel.occupies, st.roadway): while moving (not drv.motion.complete_halt) on the roadway and off the path, it moves across a lane (st.lane, as a carrier of a direction only, never a half of the roadway) or the roadway it occupies (drv.motion.moving_across_carrier, 'Road user a moves across the designated direction of travel of carrier region r'), as it does when crossing to or from the path; travelling along the roadway instead of the path is what the words forbid.

operationalizations.convention: A bicycle path is usable where its width (st.lane_width) is at least the operating width of one rider, p.usable_path_width_min (AASHTO Guide for the Development of Bicycle Facilities), and no device closes it: no dev.regulatory_sign of code closed_to_traffic or bicycles_prohibited and no dev.temporary_traffic_control governs it (dev.governs).

applicability: The subject is a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter in controlled motion (not drv.motion.complete_halt with speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance) whose footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) a roadway or a bicycle lane or path that lies on a highway h (st.on_way, st.highway) on which both a roadway and a usable bicycle lane or path p lie: p's width (st.lane_width) is at least p.usable_path_width_min and no dev.regulatory_sign of code closed_to_traffic or bicycles_prohibited and no dev.temporary_traffic_control governs p (dev.governs).
obligation: At every such observation, re-binding h and p with the whole selection: where the subject occupies a roadway lying on h and occupies no such usable path p, it moves across a lane or the roadway it occupies (drv.motion.moving_across_carrier with speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance and cos_max p.rider_crossing_motion_cos); travelling along the roadway (moving, not across) off the path is violated; on the path is compliant.

narrowings.why: 'has been provided' is read from the path's presence on the map.
'riders' is read through the machine's controlled motion.

'use the roadway' is read as travelling along it (moving, not across the occupied carrier's direction by more than p.rider_crossing_motion_cos allows); crossing the roadway to reach or leave the path is not a use of it. 'use such path' is judged where the rider would otherwise travel along the roadway: a rider elsewhere on the highway (a sidewalk) is not judged by this rule.
'usable' is read through the path's width and its closure by a device; an obstruction on the path (st.obstruction) is not read, no relation atom placing an object on a region.

param_proposals.source: AASHTO Guide for the Development of Bicycle Facilities (2012), bicyclist operating space

contract: Road user a has completed a turn to the left. Its heading change over the window behind the observation (prim.heading_change over a window of length window, degrees, positive to the left) lies in the band from turn_min inclusive to u_turn_min exclusive, so that a heading change too small to be a turn and a reversal of direction both lie outside it. The act begins within the window behind the observation at which it is recognized.
